minutes.headline: Charter committee kept the town clerk elected, dropped a second town meeting, and left section 4.2i nearly unchanged.
minutes.summary: The committee went through the draft Charter changes section by section, sorting them into grammar/legal (purple) and substantive (brown) groups and voting on each. It left the section on town facilities unchanged apart from removing the library trustees, and it kept the town clerk elected. It also dropped the second annual town meeting. Final approval waits on legal counsel's review, and the committee will keep April 10 open for another meeting.

public_comment.topic: Urged the committee to vote to change Board of Selectmen to select board rather than leave it to town meeting.

Sewer commission representative opposed the proposed change to section 4.2i, saying it would give the town manager full authority over maintenance and repair and reduce the commission's role; asked to take part in deliberations.
Said the rental language in section 4.2i is too broad and that town land use changes, such as the skateboard park at TCP, should go to a town vote.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to keep the town clerk as an elected office, leaving the Charter as is on that point.
It voted not to make the change to a second annual town meeting.
It voted to change section 4.2i only by deleting the library trustees and replacing 'his' with 'town manager'.
A motion to restore the voter-registration wording in the finance committee language failed 3-6.
The vote to recommend the Charter changes to town meeting was withdrawn and deferred until legal counsel returns the final version.

why_it_matters: The committee's recommendations shape the Charter changes that residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting, including whether the clerk is elected and how many annual town meetings are held.
The section 4.2i wording affects who manages town facilities and rentals of town property, which the sewer commission and a resident raised in public comment.
watch_next: Legal counsel's review of the Charter draft, after which the committee may vote on its recommendation.
April 10, held open for a possible further committee meeting (the chair said Monday's meeting would be cancelled).
